title: Microsoft Teams: speaker attribution in BYOD rooms is on by default, with a PowerShell setting to turn it off
summary: Hold: the cost rating says indirect costs only, although the briefing correctly identifies an add-on licence requirement for room hosts. The default, roadmap details and control instructions are supported; the briefing also appropriately flags conflicting Microsoft documentation.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new Teams AI policy setting for BYOD speaker attribution.

claims.claim: SpeakerAttributionBYOD is enabled by default.
claims.quote: This setting can be set to Enabled or Disabled, and will be enabled by default.

claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled

claims.quote: Setting to "Enabled" turns on speaker attribution in BYOD scenarios while "Disabled" will turn off the function.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls

claims.claim: A Teams admin center control for SpeakerAttributionBYOD is not documented; the Teams AI policy is PowerShell-only.
claims.quote: Searched: "SpeakerAttributionBYOD" "admin center". Opened voice-and-face-recognition, voice-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; enrollment documentation says the policy is accessible only through Microsoft PowerShell.

claims.claim: An admin UI for assigning custom Teams AI policies is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams AI policy" "assign" "admin center". Opened assign-policies-users-and-groups, settings-policies-reference, unified-policies-settings-management-teams-admin-center and voice-and-face-recognition; none gives an AI-policy assignment UI.

claims.claim: An admin UI switch for active voice enrolment is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "EnrollVoice" "admin center". Opened voice-and-face-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; also read the copilot-admin-mtr search excerpt saying there is no Teams admin center setting and PowerShell must be used.

claims.claim: The transcription setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows transcription under that meeting policy.
claims.quote:
To allow specific users in your organization to transcribe, run the following commands:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription is an existing per-organizer and per-user meeting policy setting.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams BYOD speaker recognition licensing price meter Teams Premium Copilot room host. Read voice-recognition and Teams Premium licensing; the voice-recognition BYOD requirements name Teams Premium or Copilot, with no additional qualifying host licence listed.

claims.quote: Teams Rooms and BYOD Rooms use advanced technology called speaker recognition to analyze the distinct vocal characteristics of each speaker, such as pitch, tone, and speaking style, to create a voiceprint for each participant

claims.claim: Each person has a unique voice signature stored in the organization's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud.
claims.quote: Each person gets a unique voice signature, stored securely in your organization's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud

claims.claim: A voice and face profile unused for one year is removed automatically.
claims.quote: In addition, a voice and face profile that isn't used for one year is removed automatically.

claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models or for any other purposes other than providing the voice and face recognition feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Disabling enrolment and disabling BYOD speaker attribution are distinct policy operations.
claims.quote:
EnrollVoice controls user access to active voice enrollment in the Teams app settings.
Setting to "Enabled" turns on speaker attribution in BYOD scenarios while "Disabled" will turn off the function.

claims.claim: The Low cost rating is consistent with the documented room-host add-on licensing requirement and the page's cost rationale.
claims.quote:
cost: "low"
model: "add-on"
Low. Learn ties BYOD speaker recognition to a room host holding Teams Premium or a Copilot licence; the pages read name no separate meter for this setting, so the known cost is those licences and admin time.
claims.fix: Set cost to "medium". Replace the cost rationale with: "Medium. BYOD speaker recognition requires a room host with Teams Premium or a Copilot licence, so hosts without a qualifying licence need an add-on; the cited pages name no separate meter for this setting." The assessment scale reserves low for indirect costs only and defines medium to include add-on licences for a subset of users.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the change enables clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]
